captions.detailed: This 3D model is a laboratory-style probe or ring stand featuring a wide, stable base with two parallel flat legs. An inverted V-shaped support arch rises from the back end of the legs, meeting at a rounded apex. Extending forward from this apex is a horizontal cantilever arm that terminates in a cylindrical holder with a vertical bore, designed to hold a probe, sensor, or test tube. A small horizontal screw hole is integrated into the side of the cylindrical holder to accommodate a retaining set screw.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric probe holder stand in OpenSCAD with a stable U-shaped base of parallel flat legs, an angled V-shaped support frame rising to a defined height, and a horizontal cantilever arm. The arm should end in a vertical cylindrical collar with a customizable inner radius for holding probes and a horizontal cross-hole for a retaining set screw.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a boolean union of several components, followed by a difference operation to subtract the probe bore and the set screw hole, all bounded within a bounding box intersection. The two parallel base legs are formed using cube primitives, while the angled V-shaped upright support is constructed using two hull operations that connect the leg bases to a rotated cylinder at the apex. The cantilever arm is built using a horizontal cube, and the probe holder is made from a vertical cylinder. The probe bore and screw hole are subtracted using cylinder primitives with appropriate rotations and translations.
